question: A coordinator delegates a task to a 'documentation-reviewer' subagent that should only read and comment on files, never modify them. During testing, the subagent unexpectedly edits a file it was reviewing. What configuration change prevents this?
options: A) Move the file-editing logic into the coordinator so the subagent never needs to call any tools at all
B) Add a system prompt instruction telling the subagent not to modify files, without changing its tool access
C) Lower the subagent's model tier so it is less capable of generating file-modification tool calls
D) Restrict the subagent's tools field to read-only tools like Read and Grep, omitting Edit and Write
correct_answers: D) Restrict the subagent's tools field to read-only tools like Read and Grep, omitting Edit and Write
explanations: The subagent still needs Read access to review files, so removing all tools would prevent it from doing its job rather than just preventing edits.
A prompt instruction alone is a soft constraint; if Edit and Write remain in the subagent's tool set, it can still invoke them despite the instruction.
A lower-tier model can still call Edit or Write if those tools remain available; capability level doesn't enforce a hard restriction on which tools can be invoked.
Correct. Restricting the tools field to read-only tools such as Read and Grep, and omitting Edit and Write, enforces at the configuration level that the subagent cannot modify files.
